A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ActiView and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Content can be matched despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 27 models, human evaluation, view-processing experiments, and qualitative case studies, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds model evaluations, text-only controls, and view-selection measurements. Table 11 contains results for 32 models.

M1.justification: The three pipelines and their prompt templates are substantially retained. However, v2 Section 4.1 newly permits a 'None' zooming selection, while Appendix J.2 still requires at least one selected part, as v1 did. This contradiction prevents establishing whether that procedure changed.

E1.justification: The 314 images, 325 questions, eight subclasses, and source datasets remain unchanged. v2 Appendix C adds evaluation without images under commonsense-only and forced-guessing conditions, introducing a limited new input scenario within the existing benchmark.

E2.justification: Compared with v1 Table 7, v2 Table 11 adds Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B, DeepSeek-VL-7B, DeepSeek-VL2, and Phi-3.5-Vision. The mixed-pipeline comparison expands from five to ten models, adding Claude, Gemini, both Qwen2.5 variants, and DeepSeek-VL2. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 adds selection precision and F1 alongside recall, reports selected-view counts relative to annotated counts, and introduces separate abstention-permitted and forced-guessing text-only protocols. The original image splitting, shifting difficulty settings, and human evaluation design are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a six-model ablation probing commonsense shortcuts, answer bias, and instruction-following without images. Precision/F1 also extend view-selection analysis. The splitting experiments, caption-conversion comparisons, human evaluation, and case studies already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report the random-choice baseline averaged over 10,000 runs. Neither introduces model-run uncertainty, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing. The added precision and F1 scores are evaluation metrics, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial model, selection-metric, and text-only results. Qwen2.5-VL-7B achieves 68.00% average accuracy, tying Gemini, whereas v1's best reported open-source average was 62.96%. Newly included Claude leads the mixed comparison at 72.00%. Most matched results for existing models in the appendices remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix D defines selection recall only. v2 Appendix G additionally defines false-positive views, selection precision, and F1 in Equations 1–3. These are limited mathematical additions to the evaluation definitions; no theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly presents intermediate view-selection behavior as part of the benchmark contribution and emphasizes restricted perceptual fields in the abstract. Its introduction strengthens the comparison claim by reporting open-source performance matching a leading proprietary model. The central benchmark contribution and human–model capability gap remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of text-only behavior through commonsense, training-data bias, and instruction-following, and interprets exceptions to improvements from annotated clues. Limitations add real-time manipulation and discuss reasoning models and further applications, while dropping the explicit free-form cropping future-work discussion.

D1.justification: v2 supplies exact prompts for the two text-only controls and adds backbone and vision-encoder information for new models in Table 8. Existing pipeline templates and processing details are largely retained. Both versions still describe code and data availability as forthcoming.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Phi-3, Qwen2.5-VL, DeepSeek-VL, and DeepSeek-VL2. It removes BenchLMM and the discussion distinguishing ActiView from earlier active-vision work by Ammirato and Oh. The principal positioning against static-view benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is extensively rewritten and reorganized. Detailed categories, model descriptions, pipeline explanations, and case analysis move into appendices; results gain numbered subsections; limitations become a separate main-text section. These changes substantially alter document structure beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, restructures and transposes the main results tables, adds control and comparison tables, removes Figure 1's performance-chart panel, and relocates case figures to the appendix. Most underlying example and pipeline graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The text-only controls, richer view-selection measurements, and broader model comparisons modestly strengthen benchmark validation and diagnosis. The gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: the new 'None' allowance conflicts with the retained prompt, and the general improvement claim accompanying Table 5 overlooks its exceptions. The core benchmark and most earlier evidence remain intact.
